items.description: Security-email delivery and retry operation are verified

evidence.notes: Real production delivery confirmed by querying idoc.auth_security_notification_outbox: 4 real historical rows, all sent_at populated, including two authenticator_enrolled events from this session's own real TOTP re-enrollment tests. Retry behavior for account_delivery_outbox and operational_alert_outbox was already proven by real forced-failure integration tests; auth_security_notification_outbox had no equivalent (only a source-inspection-only test for an unrelated bug), so tests/auth-security-notification-delivery.integration.ts was added, forcing a real transient failure and a real dead-letter through the actual production deliverNextAuthSecurityNotification function against real Postgres (4/4 passing).

items.description: Privileged TOTP enrollment and password/Google login are verified

evidence.notes: Operator confirmed two real production sign-ins: (1) granted the Administrator role to webmaster@idoc.club via the real /admin/members role-grant flow (fresh MFA step-up enforced), then signed in as webmaster@idoc.club with its email+password (not Google) and was correctly forced into TOTP enrollment, which was completed; (2) signed out of the zangfuqi@gmail.com super admin account and back in via Sign in with Google, and was still prompted for and completed the TOTP challenge afterward, confirming Google sign-in does not bypass MFA for a privileged account.

items.description: Ordinary password+OTP and remembered-device behavior are verified

evidence.notes: Operator completed a real production signup for marcelo@pixelsmith.space (an ordinary, non-privileged member account) after the Brevo email migration (PR #151) fixed delivery to that domain: received and entered the real 6-digit signup verification code, set a password, and completed signup. Logged out and back in with that email+password and was correctly prompted for an email OTP (not TOTP, since the account holds no privileged role); entered the code and checked 'remember this device'. Logged out and back in a second time and was NOT prompted for OTP, confirming the remembered-device cookie correctly bypassed the challenge on the same device.

items.description: Password reset and authenticator recovery/replacement are verified

evidence.notes: Operator completed both real production flows end to end: (1) password reset -- request, real emailed reset code, new password set, signed in with it; (2) authenticator replacement via recovery code -- entered a valid recovery code, set up a new authenticator, confirmed its generated code, and received the new recovery-code set. The replacement flow initially failed in production with a generic CSRF error on the confirmation step; root-caused via real Vercel logs to the general CSRF cookie's token being sourced from a root-layout React Context that Next.js can reuse (not re-render) across the client-side navigation after a Server Action redirect(), so a later stage's submitted token could legitimately drift from the current cookie. Fixed in PR #159 (merged) by giving each anonymous multi-stage continuation flow -- MFA/authenticator, login, signup, password reset -- its own per-flow csrfNonce carried in its existing signed cookie, accepted as an alternative to the general cookie. Operator retried the full authenticator-replacement flow after the fix merged and confirmed it now completes successfully. A Codex review on this evidence correctly noted docs/07 section 15.5's UAT contract for this item covers more than the happy path -- wrong/expired-code rejection, session/trust revocation and notification, privileged reset via TOTP with no email-OTP fallback, recovery-code replay rejection, and old-factor/old-code invalidation. Every one of those now has real-Postgres behavioral proof: recovery-code replay rejection, old-authenticator/old-recovery-set invalidation, session revocation, one-time code display, and acknowledgement were already proven by tests/production-mfa-finalization.integration.ts and tests/auth-recovery-adversarial.integration.ts (AUTH-RECOVERY-004/005/006 in docs/22); wrong/expired reset-code rejection, privileged TOTP-only reset with no fallback, and completion revoking every session/creating none/notifying the member were a genuine, previously-uncovered gap for the live /recover-password flow, now closed by the new tests/password-reset-adversarial.integration.ts (see docs/22 AUTH-RECOVERY-001).
